title: SpringBoneSimulator3D gravity direction is not normalized despite the documentation
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable, 4.8.dev master [5ec712e220] ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1088) - AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 47.01 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description 1. The documentation of `set_gravity_direction` says: "This value is internally normalized and then multiplied by set_gravity". 2. However, the length of the direction vector is currently multiplied into the gravity strength. That is, if y is -2, the gravity becomes twice as strong. Looking at the code, `_process_joints` multiplies the direction by gravity directly, without normalizing it (line 1830 of `scene/3d/spring_bone_simulator_3d.cpp`). 3. So the two chains in the image below should have the same shape, regardless of the direction length. I'm opening this as an issue because I'm not sure whether the code should be fixed to normalize the direction, or the documentation should be updated. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the MRP. It contains `main.tscn`. 2. There are two chains, each with its own SpringBoneSimulator3D. Both have the same gravity, 0.2; only the direction differs: (0, -1, 0) and (0, -2, 0). 3. You can see the difference right in the viewport. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp_spring_bone_gravity_direction.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33418893/mrp_spring_bone_gravity_direction.zip) It was saved with 4.7.2, but it also opens in master. Open `main.tscn` inside it.
